title: Saat Hindustani
research_notes: Filmography notes: Debut. Wikipedia's plot calls Anwar a poet from Bihar; Dustedoff places him in Ranchi, then part of Bihar. The fetched sources do not describe Anwar's fate in the mission.
character_social_background: Muslim poet from Ranchi, Bihar; fervently opposed to Hindi
role_gist: Anwar Ali is an Urdu poet from Ranchi, fervently opposed to Hindi, whose home is ransacked by anti-Urdu fanatics. He volunteers with five men of different religions and regions to join Maria, a Goan, in raising Indian flags on Portuguese forts. Sensitive and earnest, he panics when the group kills a Portuguese spy, and his comrades come to see him as a coward and the mission's weak link.
principal_motivation: Nationalist commitment to freeing Goa from Portuguese rule
principal_conflict: His fear and sensitivity against the violence of the mission, and his comrades' contempt for him; the group's own language, religious and caste prejudices
character_arc: Begins as a linguistic partisan and the suspected weak link of the group; the fetched sources do not say how his arc resolves.
critical_reception: Dustedoff (2009) found the film poorly written and directed but singled out Bachchan, who makes his presence felt as the intense, earnest and sensitive Anwar, the most interesting of the six men.
recognition: Bachchan's first acting role, as one of the seven protagonists (main Wikipedia article).

title: Anand
writers: Bimal Dutta; Gulzar; D. N. Mukherjee; Hrishikesh Mukherjee; Biren Tripathy
source_ids: SOURCE-001; SOURCE-005; SOURCE-262; SOURCE-267; SOURCE-268; SOURCE-272; SOURCE-283
research_notes: Filmography notes: Also playback singer for "Maut Tu Ek Kavita Hai". Infobox gross '₹1.7 crore' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Role type Supporting follows the film article ('supporting cast') and the main article ('supporting role in Anand'), although Bhaskar frames the story. Box Office India lists Anand on its 1970 page (gross ₹1.96 crore, nett ₹98 lakh, Semi Hit, 19th); Wikipedia's 1971 list ranks it 9th.
character_social_background: Bengali doctor in Bombay who treats the poor free of charge
role_gist: Dr. Bhaskar Banerjee, an oncologist who treats the poor free and refuses to indulge the imaginary ailments of the rich, is embittered by suffering he cannot cure. He befriends Anand, a cheerful patient with terminal cancer, who softens him and helps him win Renu. Anand dies while Bhaskar is out fetching medicine. Later Bhaskar tells Anand's story in a prize-winning book based on his diary.
principal_motivation: To heal the poor, and later to keep his dying friend alive
principal_conflict: His helplessness before disease and poverty, and his inability to save Anand
character_arc: From a withdrawn, disillusioned doctor to a man opened up by friendship and love, who keeps Anand's memory alive as an author.
character_outcome: Loses Anand; wins the blessing to marry Renu; is honoured for his book 'Anand'
critical_reception: The film article calls it a modest box-office success. The Hindu (2021) says Bachchan, in his pre-Angry Man avatar, gives a performance so subtle that it commands attention, a counterpoint to Rajesh Khanna; ThePrint calls him the perfectly stoic foil to Khanna's dramatics.
recognition: Has a cult following and is widely regarded as one of the greatest Hindi films (film article). Bachchan narrates Gulzar's poem 'Maut Tu Ek Kavita Hai'. One of only two films pairing Khanna and Bachchan, the other being Namak Haraam.

title: Pyar Ki Kahani
source_material: Remake of 1964 Tamil film Kai Kodutha Deivam
character_social_background: Well-qualified son of an Agra family whose wealth is tied up in a lawsuit, later restored
role_gist: Ram Chand, a qualified man working as a peon, saves the suicidal Ravi and takes him in as a brother. When his father's wealth is restored, his parents arrange a match with Kusum, whose reputation a spurned hoodlum has ruined with rumours. Ram meets her by chance, dismisses the gossip and accepts her, but he has promised not to marry without Ravi's approval, and Ravi, who has hidden that he is Kusum's brother, refuses.
principal_motivation: Loyalty to Ravi, and marriage to Kusum
principal_conflict: His promise to Ravi against his wish to marry Kusum after Ravi withholds approval
character_arc: A self-effacing friend whose loyalty collides with his own marriage; the resolution is not documented in the fetched sources.
critical_reception: MemsaabStory (2008) found the story ho-hum and the acting overdone, with Tanuja the film's main pleasure and Bachchan showing only flashes of charisma. Brown Car Guy (2017) felt the role, originally meant for Jeetendra, did Bachchan no favours.
research_notes: Sources disagree on the jobs: Wikipedia and Brown Car Guy make Ram the peon and Ravi the manager, while MemsaabStory says Ram gave Ravi the better post. Box Office India's 1971 list omits the film, and the main Wikipedia article counts only Bombay to Goa and Anand as pre-Zanjeer successes; no verdict entered. The ending was not found in a fetched source.

title: Parwana
producers: R. L. Suri; Jai Pawar; N. C. Sippy
role_gist: Kumar Sen, an artist who can paint, sculpt and scheme, loves Asha but cannot tell her. When she falls for the wealthy planter Rajeshwar and her uncle refuses Kumar's proposal, he builds an elaborate train-and-plane alibi, strangles the uncle and frames Rajeshwar. Asha offers to stay with Kumar if he saves Rajeshwar; realising she will always love Rajeshwar, he writes a confession and kills himself.
principal_motivation: To win Asha
principal_conflict: Asha's love for Rajeshwar and her uncle's refusal
character_arc: From a tongue-tied admirer to a calculating murderer, ending in confession and suicide.
character_outcome: Confesses to the murder, clearing Rajeshwar, and commits suicide
critical_reception: The Hindu's retrospective says the thriller made little impact on audiences but that Bachchan shone in a negative role, a daring choice so early in his career; it singles out the alibi sequence. Bachchan called it an intelligent screenplay with a many-shaded role that did not do well.
recognition: Bachchan's first antagonist role (main Wikipedia article).
research_notes: The Hindu names Asha's lover Rajesh; the Wikipedia plot and cast list name him Rajeshwar.

title: Reshma Aur Shera
character_social_background: Mute younger son of the clan chief Sagat Singh in a Rajasthan desert feud
role_gist: Chhotu, the mute sharpshooting brother of Shera, obeys his father Sagat Singh and shoots Reshma's father and newly married brother, hesitating visibly before he fires. As the feud escalates, Shera swears to kill him, and Chhotu hides in Reshma's house. The two emerge married, so Shera cannot kill him; Shera shoots himself and Reshma dies beside him.
principal_motivation: Obedience to his father, then survival
principal_conflict: Guilt over the killings against clan loyalty; his brother's vow to kill him
character_arc: From his father's obedient gunman to a hunted man who survives by marrying Reshma.
character_outcome: Survives, married to Reshma, who dies at the end
critical_reception: The film article says reviews were positive but the film was a big commercial failure. ThePrint praises its visual boldness and calls Chhotu critical to the film's emotional momentum, with Bachchan conveying guilt, confusion and religious dread through his eyes.
recognition: Reappraised as an underrated classic; ThePrint calls it Bollywood's first take on Romeo and Juliet.
research_notes: Wikipedia's 1971 list places the film 8th among top grossers, contradicting the film article and ThePrint, which call it a flop; Box Office India's 1971 list omits it. The verdict follows the film article and ThePrint. Chhotu's marriage to Reshma ends the feud, but no source treats it as a romance, so there is no Romances row. ThePrint reports Bachchan was cast as a mute because Sunil Dutt disliked his voice.

title: Sanjog
source_material: Remake of Tamil film Iru Kodugal directed by K
role_gist: Mohan marries Asha in a temple, but his mother rejects the marriage and the couple is separated. Told that Asha has died, he moves south, marries Seema and raises two children as a clerk. Asha, who bore his child, arrives years later as the new District Collector, his boss. Office rumours of an affair lead Seema to their secret; Asha dies saving her, and Mohan stays with Seema.
principal_motivation: To keep his family together
principal_conflict: His concealed first marriage, exposed when his first wife becomes his superior
character_arc: A husband who gave up his first marriage under family pressure is confronted with it ten years later and keeps his second family after the first wife's death.
character_outcome: Stays with Seema and the children, including Asha's child, after Asha's death
critical_reception: A contemporary Film World review called the screenplay old-fashioned, trite and incoherent and said the film should have stayed closer to its Tamil original. The Hindu's retrospective praises S. S. Balan's craft and Mala Sinha but finds little scope for Bachchan, calls the climax contrived and says R. D. Burman's music could not lift the box office.
recognition: Bachchan's only film with Mala Sinha (main Wikipedia article).
research_notes: Role type Co-lead: Mala Sinha is billed first and the story centres on Asha.

principal_conflict: Sharma's attempts to have Mala killed

title: Raaste Kaa Patthar
character_occupation: Junior employee at an advertising agency
character_social_background: Young bachelor in Bombay
role_gist: Jai Shankar Rai, a junior employee at Ranjeet Choudhary's advertising agency, lends his flat to his superiors for their affairs in the hope of promotion, often sleeping on the pavement outside. He rescues Neeta and gets her an audition, then falls in love with her, only to find she is involved with his married boss. When his friend Arun and Arun's wife Tanu are framed for a murder committed in his flat, Jai testifies and clears them.
principal_motivation: Career advancement, then love for Neeta and loyalty to his friend
principal_conflict: His compliance with his boss's use of his flat against his love for Neeta, whom the boss is seducing
character_arc: From a careerist who tolerates his superiors' misuse of his home to a man who takes a stand and testifies to clear his friends.
character_outcome: Testifies to clear Arun and Tanu; how his love for Neeta ends is not documented

title: Bandhe Haath
character_occupation: Thief; later poses as the writer Deepak
character_social_background: Orphan raised by the thief Madan
role_gist: Shyamu, an orphan raised as a thief by Madan, resolves to go straight after Madan's death. Fleeing Inspector Kumar, he meets Mala, a principled stage actress, while posing as the writer Deepak. Finding the real Deepak is his dying lookalike, he spares him and then takes over his identity. He wins Mala's love but must woo Deepak's pen-friend Rajni to recover incriminating letters as Kumar grows suspicious.
principal_motivation: To leave crime behind and build an honest life with Mala
principal_conflict: Keeping his stolen identity intact against Inspector Kumar's suspicion, Rajni's claims and Mala's distrust
character_arc: A thief reformed by love and conscience who spares his lookalike but sinks deeper into deception to protect his new life; the ending is not documented.

research_notes: Bachchan also plays the real Deepak, Shyamu's dying lookalike. Shyamu's feigned courtship of Rajni to recover the letters is not a romance, so it has no Romances row. The film article says it found no takers on release and recovered its cost to become 'average' fare after Zanjeer.

title: Zanjeer
production_banner: Asha Studios; Chandivali Studio; Filmistan Studio; R.K. Studios; Swati Studios
source_ids: SOURCE-001; SOURCE-020; SOURCE-265; SOURCE-267; SOURCE-270; SOURCE-277
character_social_background: Orphan who saw his parents murdered on Diwali as a child
role_gist: As a child Vijay Khanna watches a man wearing a white-horse bracelet murder his parents. Twenty years later he is an honest, brooding inspector who treats every criminal as a personal enemy. He wins over the gambling boss Sher Khan, persuades the street performer Mala to testify against crime boss Teja, and is framed and jailed. Released, he pursues revenge, learns Teja killed his parents and shoots him.
principal_motivation: Justice against Teja's syndicate and, unknowingly, revenge for his parents' murder
principal_conflict: Teja's syndicate and the frame-up that costs him his job; Mala's plea to give up vengeance
character_arc: From a traumatised, isolated officer to a man who kills his parents' murderer, throws away the bracelet and is freed of his nightmare.
character_outcome: Kills Teja, discards the zanjeer and leaves with Mala and Sher Khan
critical_reception: The Indian Express calls it a sleeper hit that displaced Rajesh Khanna and introduced the Angry Young Man, made from a Salim–Javed script three stars had turned down when romance was the dominant genre.
recognition: Established Bachchan's angry-young-man persona and began his run of Salim–Javed films (main Wikipedia article); the film article credits it with inspiring Rajinikanth and records a successful 1980 Soviet release.
research_notes: The film article reports a 1980 Soviet release with 37.3 million admissions and 9.325 million roubles (about ₹11.46 crore); kept out of Overseas Gross because it is a later release in another currency. Box Office India's gross ₹6 crore and nett ₹3 crore match the film article's labelled figures.

principal_motivation: To protect his family's good name
principal_conflict: Blackmail into crime, and the CBI investigation led by his friend Sagar
character_arc: From a loyal son covering up his father's apparent crime to a robbery accomplice who learns his father was murdered by his best friend.

writers: Nabendu Ghosh; Rajendra Singh Bedi; Biresh Chatterjee; Mohini N. Sippy; Biren Tripathy; Hrishikesh Mukherjee
source_ids: SOURCE-001; SOURCE-022; SOURCE-265; SOURCE-267; SOURCE-279; SOURCE-280

character_social_background: Established singer in Bombay
role_gist: Subir, a popular singer with no plans to marry, falls for Uma, a musically gifted village girl, marries her and brings her to Bombay, where he encourages her to sing. As his career falters and hers soars, pride and jealousy take over and the marriage breaks apart. Uma miscarries during their separation. Chastened by his aunt, Subir recognises his vanity and reconciles with her, and they sing together.
principal_motivation: His career and standing as a singer
principal_conflict: His wounded pride and jealousy when his wife outshines him
character_arc: From a confident star who promotes his wife's talent to a jealous husband who wrecks the marriage, and finally to humility and reconciliation.
character_outcome: Reconciles with Uma; they sing together
critical_reception: The film article calls it a major hit, and Saibal Chatterjee called it Bachchan's biggest hit of 1973. The BBC (2023) says many consider it among his finest roles and quotes Chatterjee that it did not force him into the masculine angry-young-man template.
recognition: Jaya Bhaduri won the Filmfare Best Actress Award. Made under the AmiYa banner named for the couple, who married about a month before release; the BBC calls it a marital drama still relevant after 50 years.

title: Saudagar
character_occupation: Date-palm juice extractor and gur trader
character_social_background: Muslim villager in rural Bengal
role_gist: Moti, a date-palm gur trader in a Bengal village, falls for Phool Banu but cannot afford her bride price. He marries the widow Majubi, whose gur makes his business famous, only to avoid paying her; once he has the money he divorces her on a false charge of infidelity and marries Phool Banu. Phool cannot make gur, his trade collapses and he beats her. Humbled, he goes back to beg Majubi's help.
principal_motivation: To marry Phool Banu and prosper in his trade
principal_conflict: His exploitation of Majubi's skill, which ruins his business once he discards her
character_arc: From a charming, calculating trader who uses one wife's labour to win another to a broken man seeking forgiveness.
character_outcome: Goes to Majubi for help and forgiveness; Majubi and Phool Banu embrace
critical_reception: ThePrint says the film explores many shades of Moti, whose selfishness toward Majubi sits beside his love for Phool Banu, while Nutan's performance dominates; it reads the film as a study of how women's labour is taken for granted.
recognition: India's official submission for the 46th Academy Awards, not nominated (ThePrint; BBC). Based on Narendranath Mitra's story Ras.
research_notes: Majubi is spelled Mahjabeen in the cast list, Majubee in the Wikipedia plot and Majubi in ThePrint. No box-office figure or verdict found.

title: Namak Haraam
writers: Gulzar; D. N. Mukherjee; Hrishikesh Mukherjee
source_ids: SOURCE-001; SOURCE-024; SOURCE-265; SOURCE-270; SOURCE-282; SOURCE-283
character_social_background: Son of the millionaire mill owner Damodar Maharaj
role_gist: Vicky, the short-tempered son of a mill owner, is forced to apologise to the union leader Bipinlal. When his father exposes Somu and has him killed, Vicky, revolted, claims to have masterminded the killing and goes to jail.
principal_motivation: Loyalty to Somu and his own pride
principal_conflict: Friendship with Somu against his father's class interests
character_arc: From a spoilt, hot-headed heir to a man who turns on his father and takes the blame for his friend's murder.
character_outcome: Jailed after taking the blame; the film opens on his release
critical_reception: Rediff (2002) says Bachchan has a definite edge over Rajesh Khanna in this clash of the titans, showing early intensity and authority, though the women remain on the fringes. ThePrint says the 'supporting' actor stole the show.
recognition: Bachchan's second Filmfare Best Supporting Actor award (film article). Retrospectively seen as marking the passing of stardom from Khanna to Bachchan (ThePrint); the two never co-starred again.

Working with the police commissioner, he poses as Prince Chandrashekar, a diamond businessman from South Africa, to get close to Digvijay, now the respectable industrialist Dharamdas, wooing Dharamdas's beloved Manju while in love with Dharamdas's sister Rinku. He finally has Dharamdas arrested.
principal_motivation: To expose the man who drove his father to suicide
principal_conflict: Digvijay Singh alias Dharamdas
character_arc: From a simple, obedient son to a disguised avenger who brings down his father's persecutor.
character_outcome: Has Dharamdas arrested.

title: Trishul
character_social_background: Illegitimate son of the construction baron R. K. Gupta, raised by his single mother Shanti
role_gist: Vijay, raised alone by Shanti after R. K. Gupta abandoned her for a wealthy marriage, comes to Delhi after her death to ruin his father. He builds Shanti Constructions, outbids Gupta, hires Gupta's wrongly dismissed secretary Geeta, tries to break up his half-brother Shekhar's romance and encourages his half-sister to defy Gupta. When Balwant Rai attacks, Gupta takes a bullet meant for Vijay, who forgives him as he dies.
principal_motivation: Revenge on the father who abandoned his mother
principal_conflict: His rivalry with R. K. Gupta and his half-brother Shekhar
character_arc: From an obsessive avenger to a son who forgives his dying father and joins his family.
character_outcome: Forgives Gupta, who dies saving him, and unites with the Gupta family; the company becomes Shanti-Raj Constructions.
critical_reception: Conversations Over Chai (blog) calls it 'Salim–Javed's script all the way' and says Bachchan and Sanjeev Kumar set the screen on fire in their confrontations, with Bachchan underplaying Vijay's hatred.
recognition: Second-highest-grossing Indian film of 1978, after Muqaddar Ka Sikandar and ahead of Don (Wikipedia).
research_notes: Wikipedia gives an Indian gross of ₹110 million and nett of ₹55 million, matching Box Office India, which adds 'Extraordinary business in Mumbai'. Hema Malini plays Shekhar's love interest. The fetched sources do not say whether Vijay and Geeta marry.

title: Muqaddar Ka Sikandar
writers: Kader Khan; Vijay Kaul; Laxmikant Sharma

role_gist: Sikandar, an orphan adopted by Fatima, has loved Kaamna since childhood, when her father Ramnath threw them out. Grown rich on rewards for turning in smugglers, he secretly pays her family's bills, but his love letter, written by his friend Vishal, makes Kaamna think Vishal loves her, and Sikandar hides his feelings as they plan to marry. Drinking and visiting the courtesan Zohra, who loves him in vain, he is mortally wounded fighting Dilawar and dies at Kaamna's wedding.

principal_conflict: His love for Kaamna, who marries his best friend

principal_conflict: His pretence of wealth and the failing business that exposes it
